jobs.description:
Please note that this position is based on our campus in Madison, WI, and requires relocation to the area. We recruit nationally and provide financial relocation assistance.

Problem-solving with a purpose.

As a Technical Solutions Engineer at Epic, you’ll work on software that impacts 305 million patients around the world. Alongside customer counterparts, you’ll tackle mission-critical and complex problems – we’re way beyond “turn it off and on again” issues. You’ll need to diagnose the problem, identify a solution, and manage the implementation of the solution, sometimes across multiple physical locations and stakeholders. Learn more about our team at https://careers.epic.com/Jobs/Technical-Solutions-Engineer.

Test the limits of your brain for the most innovative health systems on the planet.

The top-ranked health systems in U.S. News and World Report are Epic customers. Our community includes major systems like the Mayo Clinic, Johns Hopkins, Cleveland Clinic, and Kaiser Permanente, as well as leading academic medical centers at the University of Wisconsin, University of Michigan, University of California, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, and many more.

Live affordably in a city known for its rising tech talent.

Epic is located just outside Madison, Wisconsin, the second fastest growing market for tech talent in the United States and home to the state capital and the University of Wisconsin. Madison, a city surrounded by water, has received accolades for being the greenest city in America (NerdWallet), the best city for renters (SmartAsset), the fittest city in America (Fitbit), and the third best metro in the US for young professionals (Forbes Advisor).

More than just important work
.

Our uniquely themed campus was designed to heighten your ability to get stuff done in your office, a conference room, or by the fireplace in a comfy chair. All meals are restaurant-quality but cost only a few dollars, and they’re prepared by a team comprised of kitchen talent from restaurants around the country. And, after five years here, you’ll earn a four-week sabbatical anywhere in the world. Staff have kayaked in Patagonia, attended a Beyoncé concert in Ireland, built a library in Tanzania, and run a marathon in Antarctica.

We offer comprehensive benefits to keep you healthy and happy as you grow in your life and career, and your merit-based compensation will reflect the impact your work has on the company and our customers. You'll also be eligible for annual raises and bonuses, as well as stock grants, which give you an even greater stake in the success of Epic and our customers. Healthcare is global, and building the best ideas from around the world into Epic software is a point of pride. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we know that inclusive teams design software that supports the delivery of quality care for all patients, so diversity, equity, and inclusion are written into our principles. Please see our full non-discrimination statement at https://careers.epic.com/EEO.

Bachelor's degree or greater

Willingness to travel occasionally to customer locations
Eligible to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

Duration: 12+ Months

Client: Medical Device Company

Job Category: Research & Development

Employment Type: Contract on W2 (Need US Citizens Or GC Holders Only)

No H1B’s

Work hours: 40hr/ week

Remote for now, but will be expected onsite once site opens. Must be local

Preferred mathematics knowledge.
Familiarity working with large data set collection and management.
Basic understanding of chemistry

Product Stewardship Data Analyst

Job Summary

The Global Regulatory Compliance Data Analyst will collect, analyze, review, chart, enter global UDI attributes, global labelling information and global Regulatory Compliance Data information into predefined system. This position is responsible for aggregating, submitting and maintaining UDI databases which include various product data.

Additional position key elements are to provide detailed analysis, evaluation and recommendations for both UDI and Regulatory Compliance systems and process improvements, organizational development and maintenance efforts for critical challenges or issues.

Duties And Responsibilities

With supervision, participates in determination of percent composition of final and intermediate reagents as required.
Basic math/chemistry skills are required, and general knowledge of reagent process flow and SAP navigation is desired but not required.
Ensures timely and relevant development for strategies driving data attribute collection, management, entry, storage and global submission.
Compile data from multiple sources and perform report analysis in excel sheet.
Identify issues with data, gap analysis and coordinate with Product Stewardship team to ensure data standards are being maintained, identify the required changes and their priority.
Ensures that all standard data entries and summaries are statistically valid. Assists and educates users in running and interpreting results from relevant databases and reports.
Responds to internal and external requests for data through the preparation of ad-hoc queries and reports.
Collaborates with multiple stakeholders across the businesses to share project status.

Experience With Key Global Regulations

Knowledge of UN GHS (Global Harmonized System), Registration Evaluation Authorization and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH), Classification, Labelling and Packaging (CLP) Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008), Occupational Safety and Health Association (OSHA), Workplace Hazardous Material Hazardous System (WHMIS), California Proposition 65 (Cal Prop 65), European Union's (EU) Medical Device Regulation (MDR) and In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR).
Good communication skill, both verbal and written.
Able to perform multiple activities in a fast-pace environment.
Able to perform calculation on formula composition.

Qualifications

BS or BA degree in a technical, scientific, management, packaging, writing or related discipline, and minimum of 3-5 years of experience in a related field is required.
Knowledge of relevant PC software applications and possesses ability to work independently on such programs.

Must have familiarity working with large data set collection and management.
Effective communication skills, oral and written.
Demonstrated ability to influence others (beyond direct reports).
Demonstrated ability to effectively handle multiple project priorities.
Excellent organization & prioritization skills.
Demonstrated problem solving skills.
Demonstrated ability to lead dynamic work teams across functions and business units.
Project management/facilitation skills.
Excellent follow-up and documentation skills.

Job Profile Summary

Job Description

The Program Coordinator serves as the primary administrative and operational support resource for the ASU/NASPO partnership within the NASPO Department of Supply Chain Management. Reporting directly to the Department Chair, this position is responsible for coordinating partnership activities, managing communications and records, supporting events and stakeholder engagement, and assisting with departmental initiatives that advance the partnership's goals.

In addition to partnership-related responsibilities, the Program Coordinator provides support for departmental events and activities, including planning, logistics, communications, and on-site coordination for conferences, student engagement activities, faculty events, and other special programs. The position plays a key role in ensuring the successful execution of both partnership initiatives and broader departmental programming.

This role requires a high degree of initiative, independent judgment, and problem-solving. Assignments may at times be broadly defined, requiring the incumbent to independently assess situations, identify opportunities for improvement, and propose solutions that align with the objectives of NASPO, the Department of Supply Chain Management, and established ASU policies and procedures. The Program Coordinator must effectively navigate relationships with a diverse group of internal and external stakeholders, including faculty, students, university administrators, industry partners, and NASPO representatives.

The Program Coordinator is expected to operate with considerable independence while designing, implementing, coordinating, and delivering programs and initiatives that support the strategic goals of the ASU-NASPO partnership and the department. Success in this role requires strong organizational skills, sound judgment, the ability to manage competing priorities, and the capacity to develop innovative solutions in a collaborative academic environment.

Position Salary Range

$54,600 - $68,300 annually; to commensurate with education and experience.

Essential Duties

Event and Communications Support (40%)

Coordinate and manage events associated with the ASU–NASPO partnership, including meetings, conferences, lecture series, case competitions, and other collaborative initiatives.
Develop and execute event logistics, communications, scheduling, and on-site coordination to ensure successful program delivery.
Manage the Department of Supply Chain Management's NASPO-related social media presence, including platforms such as LinkedIn and Instagram, by creating and coordinating content that promotes partnership activities and student engagement.
Provide planning and operational support for departmental events, including conferences, faculty events, student engagement activities, and other special programs.

Administrative Support (30%)

Maintain records and documentation supporting the ASU–NASPO partnership, including tracking contractual deliverables, partner communications, event activities, and reporting requirements.
Coordinate meetings involving the Department Chair, NASPO Professors/Fellows, NASPO representatives, and other stakeholders.
Prepare agendas, proposals, meeting materials, correspondence, and meeting minutes as appropriate.
Serve as an administrative resource to support partnership operations and facilitate communication among internal and external stakeholders.

Student Outreach and Program Development (20%)

Collaborate with the Department Chair and NASPO representatives to develop and implement programs that enhance student engagement and experiential learning opportunities.
Support the planning, implementation, and continuous improvement of the NASPO Scholars Program.
Make recommendations for new initiatives that strengthen student participation and engagement with the ASU–NASPO partnership.

Other Duties (10%)

Perform other duties as assigned in support of departmental and partnership objectives.

Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced, service-oriented office
Experience working in a higher education environment
Demonstrated organizational skills and high attention to detail
Evidence of effective communication skills; public speaking experience preferred
Advising or customer service experience
Experience with budgetary tracking and reconciliation
Experience in working with varied populations
Experience working with confidential information or files
Demonstrated knowledge of Microsoft programs such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook
Experience working with Salesforce, Unite/admissions software, Concur, and/or event software
Collaborative, proactive, adaptable, and pragmatic

Ability to clearly communicate to perform essential functions.
